title: Impact that formed Lake El'gygytgyn
summary: Lake El'gygytgyn in central Chukotka, northeastern Siberia, occupies an impact crater about 3.6 million years old, 12 km across, with a water depth of 170 m. Researchers planned deep drilling there in 2007/08 to obtain the first continuous 3.6-million-year paleoclimate record from the terrestrial Arctic.

uncertainty.note: Source states "3.6 million year old"; no uncertainty is given. Years are Ma with no 1950 offset.
